rubric.result: The objective has two parts, and the diff has both. 'Fails only on a covered line that a file lost': dropsAgainst now returns #lineDropOf only, which is `current.covered < baseline.covered`, plus the existing missing-file entry, and compare sets exitCode 1 only from drops. 'Prints every branch difference': branchDifferences names every baseline file whose branch covered count or total differs, and compare writes that list to stdout without touching exitCode. The baseline file was regenerated. Its diff moves only two branch tallies, so the '"unstable"' key is absent.

The test the plan names is in the diff under the same name, a_file_whose_covered_lines_fall_below_its_baseline_is_a_drop_and_an_equal_count_is_not. Its baseline has 89 covered. It asserts that 88 is a drop, with the message 'src/a.ts lines covered dropped from 89 to 88', and that 89 against 89 gives []. That is exactly the boundary the plan wrote.

There is no Contract block ('No code — signatures travel in prose'). The prose contract holds: branchDifferences(baseline, measured): string[] names each file whose branches differ and gives both tallies ('from 1/2 to 2/2'); dropsAgainst names line drops and missing files only; compare writes drops to stderr with exit code 1 and differences to stdout. Both Final text blocks appear verbatim: in the ledger after 'reads each one.' with a blank line on each side, and in this-repository.md after 'says what it leaves out and why.' followed by a blank line.

The amendment of D-4 is followed. The line gate is strict for every baseline file, branches stay recorded in the baseline, and branch differences are printed and never fail. The 'A line drop' row (lines.covered lower than the baseline) is implemented as `current.covered < baseline.covered`. The 'A branch difference' row (covered or total differs) is implemented as `baseline.covered !== current.covered || baseline.total !== current.total`. 'Where the information goes' holds: stdout carries one line per file and drops go to stderr. The baseline was regenerated from one run. No feature flag was added. D-1 to D-14 are not reopened.

Files to imitate is N/A in the plan, so the module's own shape is the pattern. The new code follows it: static methods on CoverageBaseline, private #helpers that return string[], and the message style of the existing entries. The prose is in English, as CLAUDE.md requires. This skips no control of the plan and I found no clash. defects.md, rule by rule. Closed vocabulary: no subject; the diff actually removes the `Dimension` string union, and the new code adds no classifying string or boolean and no new dispatch (the verb dispatch in main is pre-existing and unchanged). Raw map as the return value of logic: the new function returns string[], not a map. It takes the `Record<string, FileCoverage>` input shape that the first plan established and the host module uses throughout, so the diff adds no new map as a return value. Two fields that have to agree: none added. #ratio's 'total === 0 means 1' convention was removed, and no sentinel was introduced. Error named for where: no new error; BaselineExists is unchanged.

The diff removes two tests: a_file_whose_line_ratio_falls_below_its_baseline_is_a_drop_and_an_equal_ratio_is_not and a_branch_drop_is_named_even_when_every_line_holds. The Tests line names both under 'Removed on purpose:', because 'Both pin the ratio rule that this task retires.' The describe title was reworded, and that is not an assertion. The other tests are untouched.

Production code produces both behaviours: #lineDropOf and #branchDifferenceOf in coverage-baseline.ts, and the stdout/stderr split in main. The tests pass literal tallies into the real CoverageBaseline methods and assert on what those methods return. No stub stands in for the comparison.

The touched paths match Files exactly: coverage-baseline.ts, coverage-baseline.test.ts, coverage-baseline.json, the ledger and this-repository.md. Nothing is missing and nothing is extra; backend/package.json dropped out of Files and is not touched. Nothing under plugin/ or frontend/ changes, the ledger.test.ts CASE finding is left alone, and no branch gate is turned on. The plan file hunk is the amendment by the plan author that the coordinating session described. It rewrites the task to the owner's final rule. Its Verification changes from `-eq 1` to `-eq 0` for '"unstable"', which follows from a rule with no unstable list and is not a loosening to make the command pass. The Tests line lists the removed tests rather than dropping promised ones.

Two tests are new. Both are deterministic: literal tallies, no clock, network or filesystem. Both are isolated: no shared state. Both verify real behaviour: with the production lines reverted, the first would get 'lines ratio dropped from 0.89 to 0.88' and fail, and the second would fail because branchDifferences would not exist and dropsAgainst would name a branch change. I report nothing beyond these three properties, so I did not load the ct-test-driven-development skill for finer findings.
